repairs.title: The Ozone Layer Is Recovering
repairs.summary: Global action phased down ozone-depleting chemicals, and the ozone layer is on a path toward recovery.
repairs.why_it_matters: It proves international environmental agreements can work when the problem is clear and enforcement is real.
repairs.caveat: Recovery is still ongoing and depends on continued compliance.

repairs.title: Smallpox Was Eradicated
repairs.summary: In 1980, the WHO declared smallpox eradicated after a global vaccination and surveillance campaign.
repairs.why_it_matters: A disease that killed millions was removed from everyday human life by organized public health work.
repairs.caveat: Smallpox is exceptional; most diseases cannot be eradicated this cleanly.

repairs.title: More Children Survive
repairs.summary: The global under-five mortality rate declined by about 60 percent between 1990 and 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: This is quiet progress measured in millions of families spared grief.
repairs.caveat: The remaining burden is still unacceptable and progress is uneven.

repairs.title: Clean Water Reached More Homes
repairs.summary: Between 2015 and 2024, 961 million people gained access to safely managed drinking water services.
repairs.why_it_matters: Better water access prevents disease and gives people time back from collecting water.
repairs.caveat: Billions still lack safely managed drinking water.

repairs.title: Extreme Poverty Fell
repairs.summary: The number of people living in extreme poverty fell from about 2.31 billion in 1990 to about 808 million in 2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: Large-scale material progress is possible, even if it is fragile and uneven.
repairs.caveat: Recent shocks and inequality mean this progress is not guaranteed to continue.

repairs.title: Literacy Became Normal
repairs.summary: Two centuries ago, only a small minority of people could read and write; today more than four out of five people can.
repairs.why_it_matters: Education changes what ordinary people can understand, build, question, and pass on.
repairs.caveat: School access and learning quality still vary sharply by region and income.

repairs.title: AIDS Deaths Fell
repairs.summary: AIDS-related deaths have fallen sharply since their peak in 2004 and are much lower than in 2010.
repairs.why_it_matters: Treatment access and sustained public health programs can turn a terrifying epidemic into a more survivable condition for many.
repairs.caveat: Funding gaps and unequal access still put lives at risk.

repairs.title: Birth Became Safer
repairs.summary: From 2000 to 2023, the global maternal mortality ratio declined by about 40 percent.
repairs.why_it_matters: Skilled care, emergency treatment, and stronger health systems save mothers' lives.
repairs.caveat: Too many preventable deaths still occur, especially where care is underfunded or disrupted.

repairs.title: Clean Power Keeps Growing
repairs.summary: Renewables supplied about 32 percent of global electricity in 2024, with the share projected to rise through 2030.
repairs.why_it_matters: The energy system is not fixed in place; infrastructure can shift when technology, policy, and cost line up.
repairs.caveat: Electricity is only part of total energy use, and grid buildout remains a serious bottleneck.

repairs.title: Leaded Petrol Ended
repairs.summary: In 2021, the last country using leaded petrol phased it out, ending legal road use worldwide.
repairs.why_it_matters: A toxic product that harmed children's brains was removed through a long, coordinated campaign.
repairs.caveat: Legacy lead pollution remains in soil, dust, and older infrastructure.

repairs.title: Air Pollution Death Rates Fell
repairs.summary: Global death rates from total air pollution have nearly halved since 1990, mainly because indoor air pollution declined.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cleaner fuels, better technology, and public health work can make invisible risks less deadly.
repairs.caveat: Outdoor air pollution remains a major global health problem.

repairs.title: Mountain Gorillas Increased
repairs.summary: Conservation work helped mountain gorilla populations recover to more than 1,000 individuals in the wild.
repairs.why_it_matters: Species decline is not always one-way when protection is persistent and local conservation works.
repairs.caveat: Mountain gorillas remain endangered and depend on continued protection.
